meaning: Two crocodiles sharing one stomach — unity in diversity, and a common destiny
note: They share a stomach and still struggle over food, because the sweetness is felt in the throat. Recorded variously as Funtummireku-Denkyemmireku (Willis) and Funtumfrafu-Denkyemfrafu (Rattray); the spelling here is the one in widest use.
references: Willis, W. Bruce. The Adinkra Dictionary: A Visual Primer on the Language of Adinkra (1998)
